09:00.headline: His offseason > one more showcase
09:00.topic: Unpopular opinion: offseason training moves the numbers; a showcase only measures them, so time showcases for when there is progress to show
09:00.caption:
Unpopular opinion: his offseason matters more than one more showcase.

A showcase is a measuring stick. It records his exit velo, 60 time, velocity or pop time on one day.

The offseason is when those numbers actually move. Strength, speed and arm work done consistently between now and spring is what gives him something new to show.

If his numbers haven't changed, another event may just confirm what coaches already saw.

That doesn't make showcases a waste. Timing matters. Measure him, train with a plan, then get re-measured when there's progress to show.

Agree or disagree? 👇

graphic.headline: His offseason > *one more showcase*
graphic.sub: A showcase measures his numbers. The work he does this winter is what changes them.

13:00.headline: Build his winter plan
13:00.topic: Four-step offseason plan: baseline test, pick 1-2 numbers, train on a schedule, retest before spring
13:00.caption:
What's your player's plan between now and spring?

Late fall and winter are quiet on the field, but they're often the best stretch of the year to improve the numbers coaches look at.

A simple four-step winter plan:

1️⃣ Test his numbers now: exit velo, 60 time, velocity or pop time, plus his grades.
2️⃣ Pick one or two to improve. Focus beats trying to fix everything at once.
3️⃣ Train on a set schedule, and keep it realistic around school.
4️⃣ Retest before spring so you know what changed.

A baseline today makes it much easier to show coaches real progress later.

Which number is he working on this winter? 👇
